sn36.22:0.3: The Theme of the Hundred and Eight
sn36.22:1.1: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you a Dhamma exposition on the theme of the hundred and eight.
sn36.22:1.3: “And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma exposition on the theme of the hundred and eight?
sn36.22:1.4: I have spoken of two kinds of feelings by one method of exposition; I have spoken of three kinds of feelings by another method of exposition; I have spoken of five kinds of feelings … six kinds of feelings … eighteen kinds of feelings … thirty-six kinds of feelings by another method of exposition; and I have spoken of one hundred and eight kinds of feelings by still another method of exposition.
sn36.22:2.1: “And what, bhikkhus, are the two kinds of feelings?
sn36.22:2.3: These are called the two kinds of feelings.
sn36.22:2.4: “And what, bhikkhus, are the three kinds of feelings?
sn36.22:2.5: Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
sn36.22:2.6: These are called the three kinds of feelings.
sn36.22:2.7: And what, bhikkhus, are the five kinds of feelings?
sn36.22:2.8: The pleasure faculty, the pain faculty, the joy faculty, the displeasure faculty, the equanimity faculty.
sn36.22:2.9: These are called the five kinds of feelings.
sn36.22:2.10: “And what, bhikkhus, are the six kinds of feelings?
sn36.22:2.11: Feeling born of eye-contact … feeling born of mind-contact.
sn36.22:2.12: These are called the six kinds of feeling.
sn36.22:2.14: “And what, bhikkhus, are the eighteen kinds of feelings?
sn36.22:2.15: Six examinations accompanied by joy, six examinations accompanied by displeasure, six examinations accompanied by equanimity.
sn36.22:2.16: These are called the eighteen kinds of feelings.
sn36.22:2.17: “And what, bhikkhus, are the thirty-six kinds of feelings?
sn36.22:2.18: Six types of joy based on the household life, six types of joy based on renunciation; six types of displeasure based on the household life, six types of displeasure based on renunciation; six types of equanimity based on the household life, six types of equanimity based on renunciation. These are called the thirty-six kinds of feelings.
sn36.22:2.20: “And what, bhikkhus, are the hundred and eight kinds of feelings?
sn36.22:2.21: The above thirty-six feelings in the past, the above thirty-six feelings in the future, the above thirty-six feelings at present.
sn36.22:2.22: These are called the hundred and eight kinds of feelings.
sn36.22:2.23: “This, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma exposition on the theme of the hundred and eight.”
